title: Pennsylvania House of Representatives District 13 Election, 2026
description: The general election for Pennsylvania's 13th House District pits Republican incumbent John Lawrence against Democratic challenger Madelyn G Alvarino. The district covers portions of Chester County in southeastern Pennsylvania and has a slight Republican lean (R+4.7 based on 2024 presidential results). Lawrence has held the seat since 2010 and is known for his focus on agricultural issues, government reform, and fiscal conservatism. Alvarino, a teacher and community advocate, is campaigning on expanding healthcare access, protecting women's rights, and gun safety, aiming to flip a district that Democrats view as potentially competitive in the current political environment.

candidates.name: John A. Lawrence
candidates.summary: John Lawrence is the incumbent Republican member of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives for District 13, first elected in 2010. A lifelong resident of southern Chester County, he chairs the Commerce Committee and serves as vice chair of Agriculture & Rural Affairs, with a focus on government reform, agricultural policy, and fiscal responsibility. Lawrence declines a state pension and per diems, and has authored legislation on dairy industry support, wastewater utility regulation, and government transparency.

candidates.name: Madelyn G Alvarino
candidates.summary: Madelyn Alvarino is the Democratic candidate for Pennsylvania House of Representatives District 13. She is an educator and community member who has lived in the district since 1999, running on a platform that emphasizes healthcare access, reproductive rights, gun safety, and affordability. Alvarino has been endorsed by the Chester County Democrats, Committee to Protect Health Care, Gun Sense Voter, New American Leaders Action Fund, and Represent PA.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific public polling exists for this race as of mid-2026, so this forecast relies on structural factors rather than direct voter measurement. The district has a Republican lean of R+4.7 based on 2024 presidential results. Incumbent John Lawrence has held the seat since 2010, adding a meaningful incumbency advantage through 16 years of service, committee leadership (Commerce Chair, Agriculture & Rural Affairs Vice Chair), and demonstrated electoral durability. Democratic challenger Madelyn Alvarino is a credible candidate with several endorsements, and the district is described as potentially competitive, which tempers the Republican rating. However, absent polling and in a district with a clear Republican structural edge plus a long-serving incumbent, Republicans hold a meaningful advantage. The low confidence reflects the absence of polling data.
